chunks: 10. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, from Mu'adh al-Jawhari, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, blessings of Allah be upon them, from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), from Jibra'il (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah, great be His Glory, said: Whoever commits a sin, minor or major, and he does not know that I have the right to punish him for it or to forgive him, I will never forgive him that sin. And whoever commits a sin, whether minor or major, and he knows that I have the right to punish him and to forgive him, I forgive him.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for God's forgiveness of sins according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this Hadith Qudsi clarifies the theological mechanism of divine mercy by linking forgiveness to the sinner's conscious recognition of God's absolute authority (Hujjah) over punishment and pardon. It highlights that true repentance requires not just the act, but the internal conviction of God's capacity to both exact retribution and grant clemency, a concept central to Shia discussions on divine justice and grace.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 10. My father (RA) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of Mu`adh al-Jawhari, on the authority of al-Sadiq Ja`far ibn Muhammad (AS), on the authority of is forefather, blessings of Allah be upon them that The Messenger of Allah (SA) said: Jibra`il (AS) said:

Allah, great be His Glory said: Whoever commits a sin, major or minor, and he does not believe that I have a right to punish him over it or to forgive for it, then I will never forgive him for that sin ever. Whoever commits a sin, whether be it minor or major, believing that I have a right to punish him over it or forgive for it, I forgive him.
